subject: Investigation: Coordinated resubmission of eval credits — KiteWave
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Possible coordinated resubmissions from KiteWave — need quick eyes

Team,

I flagged a pattern that looks like the same org submitting trial/extension requests across multiple accounts and contact emails. Attached is an extract (kitewave_audit_extract.csv) with timestamps, IPs, and request payload ids. Highlights: three distinct accounts created within 48 hours, identical billing tokens, and two separate extension requests approved within 12 hours of each other.

Quick ask: can we confirm whether these map to independent KiteWave teams or a single group re-submitting? If this is abuse we should pause further eval credits and notify CS/Legal.

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Sales Ops 
Redwood Inference
[attachment: kitewave_audit_extract.csv (CSV, 22 KB)]

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-09T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Possible coordinated resubmissions from KiteWave — need quick eyes

Ben — good catch.

I skimmed the CSV. The billing token overlap is the big red flag; it suggests the same payment instrument is being reused. Neha, can you cross-reference with prior pilot approvals (HUBSPOT-REC-48291) and check whether these accounts have any SSO or domain ownership overlap? Lauren, please stand by to draft a suspension notice if we decide to hold credits.

Until we confirm, do not approve any more manual credit grants for KiteWave. Ben — please also pull the demo-scheduling notes to see if the CSMs treated these as separate teams or the same point-of-contact.

I'll loop Legal if evidence confirms coordinated resubmission.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Samir Patel <samir@kitewave.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@kitewave.com
Date: 2026-08-09T12:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Investigation: Coordinated resubmission of eval credits — KiteWave

Marcus — thanks for the heads up. I wanted to clarify from our side: KiteWave has three independent product teams running parallel pilots (Search, Routing, and Insights). Each has its own project budget and POC. They asked the account team to request small top-ups because their evaluation windows barely overlapped with internal team vacations.

I attached the signed request from our Procurement (customer-extension-request.pdf). If you need, I can share the PO numbers and internal approvals. We absolutely do not condone gaming credits — happy to provide whatever evidence you need to validate the distinct teams.

Regards,
Samir Patel
Head of Cloud Platform
KiteWave
[attachment: customer-extension-request.pdf (PDF, 56 KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-10T08:21:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Investigation: Coordinated resubmission of eval credits — KiteWave

Following up with the additional telemetry I pulled overnight: the three accounts share the same browser fingerprint and come from a single /24 CIDR on two of the requests. Transaction metadata shows the same device_user_agent string on two accounts. That changes the probability toward single-actor reuse versus legitimately separate teams.

I also checked our grant notes — CSM entered manual grants for two accounts after the second support ticket. The grant ids are GNT-99811 and GNT-99812. I've put a redacted snapshot in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/KiteWave/cred-audit-20260809

My recommendation: temporarily suspend further eval credits for all KiteWave accounts and open a short inquiry with the customer asking for PO/approval evidence for each team before additional grants. If they furnish unique POs and distinct billing agents, we can re-evaluate.

-Ben

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>, Legal <legal@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-11T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Action: suspend eval credits pending evidence — KiteWave (urgent)

Team — based on Ben's telemetry and the billing-token reuse, we will suspend additional eval credit approvals for KiteWave effective immediately. Lauren, please send the following to Samir (cc: ops@kitewave.com): a short notice explaining the temporary hold, and a request for PO numbers or procurement emails for each claimed team. Use the template linked below and ask for documentation within 5 business days.

Legal — tagging you to confirm the wording. If KiteWave responds with clear distinct POs and unique billing agents, we can reopen grants on a case-by-case basis. If they do not provide evidence, we'll escalate to contract evaluation and consider recovery of previously issued credits (GNT-99811, GNT-99812).

Link to template and evidence folder: https://drive.redwood.internal/shared/KiteWave/cred-audit-20260809
HubSpot record: HUBSPOT-REC-48291

I'll draft the notice now; Lauren, please push the message by EOD.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Sr. Revenue Ops Manager
Redwood Inference
